h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Knox County, TN
hero_subtitle: From the ridges around House Mountain to the subdivisions of Hardin Valley, get matched with up to 3 licensed, insured roofers who work across Knox County.
intro: Knox County sits in classic Ridge-and-Valley country, where Sharp's Ridge, Beaver Ridge and Copper Ridge run northeast to southwest between settled valleys. The Holston and French Broad rivers meet at Forks-of-the-River to form the Tennessee, and House Mountain near Corryton tops out around 2,064 feet. Inside that terrain is nearly every kind of roof East Tennessee has: early 1900s houses in Knoxville's older neighborhoods, postwar ranches, homes along Fort Loudoun and Melton Hill lakes, and newer subdivisions spreading through Karns, Powell and Hardin Valley.

sections.heading: Three permitting offices and a county license rule
body: Before work starts, it helps to know which local government covers your address. Knox County Codes Administration approves plans and issues building permits for areas of the county outside Knoxville city limits. The City of Knoxville runs its own permitting, and the Town of Farragut has its own building official and codes staff. A roofer who works the whole county should know which office applies to your street and whether your particular job needs a permit.

Licensing is the other piece. Knox County is one of nine Tennessee counties that adopted the state's home improvement law, so residential projects from $3,000 to $24,999, roofing included, must be done by a contractor holding a Home Improvement license. Jobs of $25,000 or more require a state contractor's license. Ask for the license number and look it up with the Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors before you sign.

sections.heading: From Fourth and Gill to Hardin Valley
body: Knox County's housing spans more than a century. Knoxville's H-1 historic overlays, including Old North Knoxville, Fourth and Gill and Mechanicsville, hold Victorian and Craftsman houses, and exterior work there needs a certificate of appropriateness from the Knoxville Historic Zoning Commission. Commission records show even like-for-like asphalt shingle replacements in those neighborhoods going through staff-level certificates.

Beyond the older core, most housing is postwar or newer: ranch homes in Fountain City and Bearden, then larger subdivisions along the Pellissippi Parkway corridor and north toward Powell and Halls Crossroads. If your subdivision has a homeowners association, read its covenants for shingle color or material rules before you settle on a quote.

sections.heading: Storms that have hit Knox County roofs
body: On August 7, 2023, the National Weather Service confirmed an EF-2 tornado in western Knox County with estimated peak winds of 130 mph. It began near Yarnell Road and North Campbell Station Road, caused significant roof damage to homes in the Lovell Cove subdivision, crossed Pellissippi Parkway between Farragut and Karns, and dissipated near Bob Gray Road and Middlebrook Pike.

More routine threats are spring hail, falling trees and the occasional heavy snow. In May 2023, the NWS logged hail up to an inch near Corryton and Maloneyville. In January 2024, reports across the county ranged from 7 to nearly 10 inches of snow, and Knoxville kept 4 inches or more on the ground for seven straight days, the longest such stretch in records back to 1910.

faqs.q: Does a roofer need a special license to work on my Knox County home?
faqs.a: For most replacements, yes. Knox County adopted Tennessee's home improvement law, so residential projects from $3,000 to $24,999, including roofing, require a contractor with a Home Improvement license. Work costing $25,000 or more needs a state contractor's license. You can look up any license number through the Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors before signing.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits for a roof in Knox County?
faqs.a: That depends on your address. Knox County Codes Administration handles plan approval and building permits for areas outside Knoxville city limits, the City of Knoxville runs its own permitting, and the Town of Farragut has its own building official. Ask the roofer to confirm with the right office whether your job needs a permit and who will pull it.

faqs.q: My house is in Old North Knoxville or Fourth and Gill. Can I just replace the shingles?
faqs.a: Not without paperwork. Properties in Knoxville's H-1 historic overlays need a certificate of appropriateness from the Knoxville Historic Zoning Commission for exterior work. Commission records show routine in-kind shingle replacements in Fourth and Gill and Old North Knoxville approved at staff level, and each district has design guidelines that address roofs. Build that step into your timeline.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Blount County, TN
hero_subtitle: Foothill cabins, homes near Fort Loudoun Lake and neighborhoods in Maryville and Alcoa: compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers serving Blount County.
intro: Blount County runs from Fort Loudoun Lake on its northern edge to Thunderhead Mountain, its highest point at 5,527 feet, inside Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Chilhowee Mountain crosses the middle of the county and marks the geologic line between the Ridge-and-Valley and the Blue Ridge. That split shapes roofing here: suburban streets around Maryville and Alcoa on one side, and coves, cabins and steep wooded lots around Townsend, Walland and Happy Valley on the other.

sections.heading: Mountain-wave winds along the foothills
body: The western foothills of the Smokies get a particular kind of windstorm. When strong winds cross the mountains, air can race down the slopes in what forecasters call a mountain wave, and NWS Morristown research finds these events most often from November through March. During the March 30, 2022 event, a park wind tower at Look Rock on Chilhowee Mountain measured a 77 mph gust, and the airport sensor near Alcoa recorded 64 mph.

Gusts like that tend to start at roof edges, rakes and ridge caps. For a foothill home, it is worth asking a roofer about wind-rated shingles, the fastening pattern at the edges, and whether metal makes sense for your pitch and exposure.

sections.heading: Cabins in Townsend and Walland
body: Townsend sits in Tuckaleechee Cove at about 1,076 feet and calls itself the Peaceful Side of the Smokies, with U.S. 321, the Lamar Alexander Parkway, linking it to Walland and Maryville. The town grew from the Little River Lumber Company, founded in 1901, and tourism has kept the cove busy since the national park opened. Cabins set against wooded slopes are a common sight.

Cabin roofs raise their own questions: heavy shade that keeps shingles damp, leaves packing into valleys, steep or narrow drives that limit where a dumpster can sit, and, for rentals, timing work between guest stays. Bring those details up when roofers call.

sections.heading: Lake towns and the western county
body: Along the northern edge, Fort Loudoun Lake forms Louisville's border. The town was a flatboat and steamboat port when it incorporated in 1851 and has grown quickly in recent years. Friendsville, founded by Quakers from North Carolina in the 1790s, stretches from the lake south toward U.S. 321, with farms and newer homes along Miser Station Road.

For permits, Blount County Development Services enforces the 2018 edition of the International Code Council's residential and commercial codes and takes applications for construction permits. If you live inside Maryville, Alcoa or another city, have your roofer confirm which office handles your address.

roofing_notes: Foothill homes near Chilhowee Mountain see mountain-wave gusts, mostly from November through March.
Shaded cabin lots stay damp; ask about leaf-filled valleys, moss and attic ventilation.
For rental cabins, schedule tear-off between bookings and confirm nail cleanup on drives.
Blount County Development Services enforces the 2018 International Code Council codes.

faqs.q: Why do roofs near Walland and Happy Valley take such a beating from wind?
faqs.a: These communities sit in the western foothills of the Smokies, where mountain-wave winds can roar downslope, mostly between November and March. On March 30, 2022, a park wind tower at Look Rock recorded a 77 mph gust. A roofer should check edges, ridge caps and fastening, since wind usually gets a grip at those points first.

faqs.q: What building code applies in Blount County?
faqs.a: Blount County Development Services says it enforces the commercial and residential regulations of the 2018 edition of the International Code Council through plan review and inspections, and it accepts applications for construction permits. If your home is inside a city such as Maryville or Alcoa, ask your roofer to confirm with the correct office whether a permit is needed.

faqs.q: Can roofers get materials up to a mountain cabin outside Townsend?
faqs.a: Usually, but access shapes the quote. Narrow gravel drives, switchbacks and tight turnarounds may mean smaller trucks, hand-carrying bundles or a slower tear-off. Send photos of the driveway and roof when roofers contact you, and mention whether the cabin is rented so the work can be planned between stays.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Anderson County, TN
hero_subtitle: From Norris Lake cabins to TVA-era homes in Norris and older houses around Rocky Top, compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers serving Anderson County.
intro: Federal projects shaped Anderson County's housing as much as the land did. The Tennessee Valley Authority built Norris Dam on the Clinch River from 1933 to 1936 and laid out the town of Norris to house its workers, and in 1942 the Manhattan Project brought Oak Ridge. North of Clinton the ground rises toward the Cumberland Mountains and former coal communities such as Briceville and Rocky Top, while Andersonville sits just south of Norris Lake and its wooded coves.

sections.heading: Norris, the planned TVA town
body: Norris was built in 1933 as a model planned community, with winding roads that follow the terrain, a central green and a surrounding greenbelt borrowed from England's garden city movement. Its houses came from twelve basic designs, each with a porch and fireplace, built of local wood and stone, and many were among the first all-electric homes. The town has been on the National Register of Historic Places as the Norris District since 1975.

Reroofing one of these houses calls for some care. Framing and decking from the 1930s may not match modern lumber sizes, chimneys need sound flashing, and you may want a material that keeps the original look. Check with the City of Norris about any local requirements before you choose.

sections.heading: Coal towns north of Clinton
body: Rocky Top, known first as Coal Creek and then as Lake City before taking its current name in 2014, straddles the Anderson and Campbell county line along Interstate 75. Nearby Briceville is another former mining community, and the North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area reaches into the county's rugged northern end.

Hillside lots, older frame houses and manufactured homes are all part of the mix up here. An older roof may hide more than one layer of shingles that has to come off before new material goes on, so ask whether each quote assumes a full tear-off.

sections.heading: Weather in the Clinch River valley
body: Clinton sits on a stretch of the Clinch River that is technically part of Melton Hill Lake, with State Route 61 running northeast to Norris and Andersonville. On May 16, 2023, the National Weather Service logged 1-inch hail five miles southwest of Clinton and hail up to an inch northeast of Oak Ridge. During the January 2024 snowstorm, a spot two miles northwest of Clinton measured 10 inches.
After hail, ask a roofer to check soft metals such as vents, flashing and gutters, along with shingle bruising and granule loss, and photograph anything they find before you call your insurer.

roofing_notes: Norris is a National Register historic district; check with the city before changing roof materials.
Cabins near Andersonville and Norris Lake can have tight access for trucks and dumpsters.
Older homes in former mining towns may hide several shingle layers or worn decking.
Inch-size hail was reported near Clinton and Oak Ridge in May 2023.

faqs.q: I own one of the original houses in Norris. What should I tell a roofer?
faqs.a: Tell them the house is in the Norris District, the TVA-built town listed on the National Register in 1975. The original houses used local wood and stone and each had a fireplace, so expect chimney flashing to need attention. Ask about decking condition, whether the material suits the house, and check with the City of Norris about local requirements.

faqs.q: Does Anderson County get damaging hail?
faqs.a: It happens. During the May 16, 2023 storms, the National Weather Service received reports of 1-inch hail five miles southwest of Clinton and hail from 0.7 to 1 inch about six miles northeast of Oak Ridge. Stones that size can bruise shingles and dent metal vents, so an inspection is worth scheduling even when nothing is leaking.

faqs.q: Can I get quotes for a lake cabin near Andersonville?
faqs.a: Yes. Requests are welcome from anywhere in Anderson County, including Andersonville, Norris, Briceville and Rocky Top. For a cabin on a Norris Lake cove, describe how steep the access is and whether materials must be carried down to the house, because that affects labor and the final price.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Loudon County, TN
hero_subtitle: Lake homes on Tellico and Fort Loudoun, farm country around Greenback and Philadelphia, and growing Lenoir City: get up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers.
intro: Water defines Loudon County. The Little Tennessee River meets the Tennessee at Lenoir City, Fort Loudoun Dam holds back Fort Loudoun Lake, Tellico Dam forms Tellico Lake, and below the dam the river becomes part of Watts Bar Lake. About 18 of the county's 247 square miles are water. Growth has been steady too, from about 39,000 residents in 2000 to nearly 55,000 in 2020, so local roofers work on everything from older homes in Loudon to lakefront houses and new subdivisions.

sections.heading: Planned lake communities
body: Tellico Village, on the western shore of Tellico Lake about 30 miles southwest of Knoxville, was established by Cooper Communities in 1986 as a planned retirement community with three golf courses, and its governmental functions are handled by the Tellico Village Property Owners Association. Rarity Bay, which reaches into Monroe County, is another lakeside community counted as its own census-designated place.

In communities like these, association rules can matter as much as the building code. Get the current approval requirements before comparing prices, then give each roofer the exact shingle line and color you plan to submit so every quote covers the same product.

sections.heading: Big hail in the river valley
body: Loudon County has seen serious hail. During the May 6, 2022 storms, the National Weather Service received reports of golf ball to lime-sized hail, 1.75 to 2 inches across, in the county, with damage photographed in Lenoir City. Radar estimates in that storm showed stones of 2 inches or more.
Hail that large can crack shingles, dent gutters and break skylights. If your neighborhood was hit, request an inspection with photos and keep a note of the storm date for your insurer.

sections.heading: Older towns and open farmland
body: Loudon, the county seat, was settled in the 1790s and incorporated in 1850 on the Tennessee River. Lenoir City was platted in the 1890s after the railroad brought growth. Older houses in both towns may have original board decking, chimneys and porch roofs that need separate attention in a quote.

South of the lakes, Greenback and Philadelphia are small cities surrounded by farmland, where a property may include a barn or equipment shed along with the house. U.S. 321 links Lenoir City east to Blount County, and Interstate 75 crosses the county on its way toward Sweetwater.

roofing_notes: Get POA or HOA approval requirements before comparing bids in planned lake communities.
Hail of 1.75 to 2 inches was reported in the county in May 2022; check skylights and gutters after storms.
Lakefront roofs catch wind across open water; ask about edge metal and fastening.
Farm properties may need separate line items for barns and outbuildings.

faqs.q: Does Tellico Village have to approve a new roof?
faqs.a: Tellico Village's governmental functions are managed by its Property Owners Association, so check with the association for its current architectural requirements before you sign a contract. Share any approval rules, such as color or material limits, with every roofer who quotes so the bids are comparable and the job is not held up waiting on paperwork.

faqs.q: How big has hail gotten in Loudon County?
faqs.a: On May 6, 2022, the National Weather Service received reports of golf ball to lime-sized hail, roughly 1.75 to 2 inches, in Loudon County, and radar estimated stones of 2 inches or more. Hail that large can fracture shingles and dent metal, so an inspection makes sense after any storm with hail reported near Lenoir City or Loudon.

faqs.q: I have a house on Fort Loudoun or Tellico Lake. What should I ask roofers?
faqs.a: Ask how the roof will be fastened at the edges and ridge for wind coming across the water, which underlayment they recommend, and how they will keep nails and debris out of the lake, dock and boat lift. If the only access is a steep drive, ask whether that changes the price or schedule.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Sevier County, TN
hero_subtitle: Whether it's a full-time home in Kodak or a rental cabin above Wears Valley, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers who work in Sevier County.
intro: Sevier County climbs from the French Broad River and Douglas Lake in the north to Kuwohi, formerly Clingmans Dome, at 6,643 feet on the North Carolina line. The three forks of the Little Pigeon River run north out of the Smokies and converge near Sevierville. After the national park ended large-scale logging, tourism took over the economy, and the cabin rental business has grown tremendously. The result is a roofing mix unlike anywhere nearby: mountain cabins, condos, farmhouses and suburban homes.

sections.heading: Wildfire and the wooded ridges
body: Two wildfires have shown how exposed the county's wooded ridges can be. In late November 2016, the Chimney Tops 2 fire was driven into Gatlinburg by extreme winds; 14 people died, and county officials put the toll at about 2,460 structures damaged or destroyed. On March 30, 2022, the Hatcher Mountain fire near Wears Valley burned more than 3,000 acres and damaged over 100 homes during a high-end mountain-wave wind event.

For a cabin tucked into the trees, the roof is part of fire planning. Ask roofers about Class A fire-rated roof assemblies, how vents and edges are detailed, and keeping leaves and needles out of valleys and gutters, where embers can land.

sections.heading: Wind off Cove Mountain
body: The same downslope winds that fanned those fires hit roofs on their own. During the 2022 event, a park wind tower on Cove Mountain, about three miles east-southeast of Wears Valley, recorded an 85 mph gust. NWS Morristown research has identified Cove Mountain as one of the windiest spots during these foothill windstorms, which come mostly from November through March.

On August 7, 2023, straight-line winds estimated up to 85 mph also cut a 12-mile path from Kodak toward Dandridge, damaging a marina roof on Douglas Lake and tearing RV canopies from their anchors. Ridge caps, edge fastening and how metal panels are attached deserve close attention here.

sections.heading: Roofing a rental cabin
body: Many Sevier County roofs sit over vacation rentals, where a leak can cost bookings. Steep lots off Wears Valley Road, the hills around Pigeon Forge and the ridges above Gatlinburg often mean narrow drives, little room to stage materials and roofs that are awkward to reach.

When requesting quotes for a rental, tell roofers your booking calendar, whether a property manager will be the contact, and how materials can get to the house. Written start and finish dates help you block the right nights.

roofing_notes: Ask about Class A fire-rated roof assemblies for cabins surrounded by woods.
Cove Mountain recorded an 85 mph gust in March 2022, so fastening details matter.
Coordinate rental cabin work around guest bookings and property managers.
Steep, narrow drives can affect equipment, dumpster placement and labor costs.

faqs.q: Should I choose a fire-resistant roof for my cabin?
faqs.a: It is worth discussing. Sevier County has lived through the 2016 Chimney Tops 2 fire and the 2022 Hatcher Mountain fire near Wears Valley, both pushed by strong winds. Ask roofers about Class A fire-rated roof assemblies, keeping gutters and valleys clear of leaves, and how edges and vents are detailed to resist embers. Your insurer may have recommendations too.

faqs.q: How windy does it get in Wears Valley?
faqs.a: Very windy at times. Mountain-wave events push air down the north side of the Smokies, mostly from November through March. Early on March 31, 2022, a park wind tower at Cove Mountain, a few miles east-southeast of Wears Valley, recorded an 85 mph gust. A roofer should explain how shingles or metal panels will be fastened for that kind of exposure.

faqs.q: Can work on a rental cabin be scheduled between guests?
faqs.a: Often, yes, with some planning. Tear-off, weather and steep access can stretch a cabin job past a single day, so share your booking calendar when roofers contact you, ask for a written schedule, and agree on who lets the crew in and checks the drive for stray nails before the next guests arrive.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Jefferson County, TN
hero_subtitle: Between Douglas Lake and Cherokee Lake, from historic Dandridge to Jefferson City and White Pine, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers.
intro: Jefferson County sits between two TVA reservoirs: Douglas Lake on the French Broad River to the south and Cherokee Lake on the Holston to the north. Water covers about 13 percent of its 314 square miles. Dandridge, the county seat, was settled in 1783, and most of its downtown lies below Douglas Lake's high-water mark behind a levee TVA built after residents appealed to Washington. Jefferson City, White Pine and New Market fill out a county of lake houses, small-town streets and farmland crossed by I-40 and I-81.

sections.heading: Living on Douglas and Cherokee lakes
body: Douglas Lake's shoreline runs past Dandridge, the resort community of Baneberry and the southern edge of White Pine, while Jefferson City's northwestern edge touches the southern arm of Cherokee Lake. Homes along these shores catch wind across open water, and the August 7, 2023 storm showed how hard that can be: surveyors traced 12 miles of straight-line wind damage, estimated up to 85 mph, from Kodak to east of Dandridge.
For a lake home, ask about wind-rated shingles or metal, ridge vents that hold up to wind-driven rain, and how the crew will protect docks, boats and landscaping during tear-off.

sections.heading: Small tornadoes and strong gusts
body: On January 12, 2023, two brief EF-0 tornadoes touched down in the county, one west of Dandridge across Deep Springs Road and one southeast of Baneberry near Harrison Ferry Road that crossed U.S. 25E. A trained spotter southwest of Dandridge measured a 60 mph gust and reported shingles missing from a roof. In December 2021, wind damaged a mobile home in New Market.

Events like these more often call for repairs than full replacements, but missing shingles let water in quickly. If you find tabs in the yard after a storm, get the roof patched or tarped before the next rain and keep photos for your insurer.

sections.heading: Historic Dandridge and older town centers
body: Dandridge was named for Martha Dandridge Washington, a point residents made when they asked Eleanor Roosevelt for help as TVA planned Douglas Dam in the 1940s. The agency built a levee, and the historic downtown survived.

White Pine, first called Dandridge Crossing and renamed in 1873, rebuilt its downtown after a 1905 fire, and Jefferson City grew from the Mossy Creek settlement around Carson-Newman, founded in 1851. Older houses in these towns can have steep pitches, porch roofs and chimneys that need careful flashing work.

January 2023 EF-0 tornadoes near Dandridge and Baneberry came with reports of missing shingles.
Older homes in Dandridge, White Pine and Jefferson City may need chimney and porch-roof flashing work.

faqs.q: Has Jefferson County had tornadoes recently?
faqs.a: Yes. On January 12, 2023, the National Weather Service confirmed two EF-0 tornadoes, one west of Dandridge near Deep Springs Road and another southeast of Baneberry that crossed U.S. 25E. The same storms brought a measured 60 mph gust southwest of Dandridge, where shingles were reported missing from a roof.

faqs.q: I live on Douglas Lake. What should I ask roofers?
faqs.a: Ask how the roof will be fastened for wind off the water, which underlayment and ridge vent they recommend against wind-driven rain, and how they will keep debris off docks, boats and the shoreline. If your home is in a community such as Baneberry, check any association rules on materials or colors first.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Roane County, TN
hero_subtitle: Victorian homes in Harriman, lake houses on Watts Bar and hillside homes below Walden Ridge: compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers in Roane County.
intro: Roane County straddles the boundary between the Tennessee Valley and the Cumberland Plateau, and the escarpment of Walden Ridge is visible from much of it. The Clinch, Emory and Tennessee rivers meet at Kingston, and most of that water now belongs to Watts Bar Lake. Each town has its own story: Kingston grew from Fort Southwest Point in the 1790s, Harriman was planned as a temperance town in 1889, and Rockwood became an iron and coal center at the foot of the ridge.

sections.heading: Harriman's historic houses
body: The East Tennessee Land Company laid out Harriman in late 1889, setting aside larger lots in what is now the Cornstalk Heights Historic District, listed on the National Register in 1991. Its Queen Anne, Colonial Revival and bungalow houses date from 1890 to 1940, and many were built by affluent residents in the 1890s and early 1900s.

Roofs on houses this age can involve steep, complex pitches, dormers, intersecting gables and tall chimneys. Ask roofers whether they have worked on homes of this era and how they handle flashing and ventilation where roof planes meet.

sections.heading: Below Walden Ridge
body: Rockwood sits at the base of the plateau's eastern escarpment at about 892 feet. The Roane Iron Company, chartered in 1867, mined coal and iron ore along the ridge and ran a blast furnace there until 1929, and Watts Bar Lake forms much of the city's southern edge.

This end of the county has taken hard wind. On June 21, 2021, Rockwood reported numerous trees and power lines down throughout the county, and a barn was destroyed. That December, another line of storms brought down multiple trees along Highway 27 south of Interstate 40. On wooded lots, have a roofer check for limb punctures after storms like these.

sections.heading: Lakeshore homes and the Oak Ridge side
body: Kingston, the county seat, briefly served as Tennessee's capital for one day in 1807, and the stacks of TVA's Kingston Fossil Plant are visible from Interstate 40. Homes on Watts Bar Lake and along the Clinch and Emory rivers face wind across open water, so edge and ridge details matter.

Roane County also includes the western part of Oak Ridge and part of Oliver Springs, and a sliver of Harriman reaches into Morgan County. When you request quotes, give the full street address so roofers know which local office handles your home.

roofing_notes: Cornstalk Heights homes, built 1890 to 1940, can have complex rooflines and tall chimneys.
Rockwood and wooded areas below Walden Ridge saw heavy tree damage in the June 2021 storms.
Watts Bar lakefront homes take wind across open water; ask about edge and ridge fastening.

faqs.q: My house is in Cornstalk Heights. Does that change the roofing job?
faqs.a: It can. Cornstalk Heights is a National Register historic district of Queen Anne, Colonial Revival and bungalow homes built between 1890 and 1940. Older roofs may have several layers, worn board decking and chimney flashing that needs rebuilding. Ask the City of Harriman whether any local review applies, and choose a roofer comfortable with older, steeper roofs.

faqs.q: Do you cover the Roane County part of Oak Ridge?
faqs.a: Yes. The western portion of Oak Ridge lies in Roane County, as do parts of Oliver Springs, and you can request free quotes there just as you would in Kingston, Harriman, Rockwood or along Watts Bar Lake. Roofers you are matched with generally get in touch within a day or two.

faqs.q: What storm damage has Roane County seen recently?
faqs.a: Mostly wind and falling trees. On June 21, 2021, Rockwood reported numerous trees and power lines down across the county, and a barn was destroyed. In December 2021, trees fell along Highway 27 near Rockwood, and in May 2024, trees and power lines were reported down around Kingston and on Highway 61 near Harriman.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Union County, TN
hero_subtitle: Farmhouses in Raccoon Valley, lake homes on the Sharps Chapel peninsula and houses along Maynardville Highway: compare up to 3 licensed, insured roofers.
intro: Union County is ridge-and-valley country. Copper Ridge, Hinds Ridge and Lone Mountain run across it, and Maynardville sits near the center of narrow Raccoon Valley, about 15 miles from Knoxville along State Route 33. The Clinch River crosses the north end as part of Norris Lake, and water makes up nearly a tenth of the county's area. When TVA's Norris Dam flooded the valley in the 1930s, towns such as Loyston disappeared and families went through what they called The Move.

sections.heading: Norris Lake homes around Sharps Chapel
body: Sharps Chapel lies on a peninsula along the northern shore of Norris Lake, with water on several sides and many waterfront subdivisions. Big Ridge State Park, where Big Ridge Dam forms a small lake off a Norris Lake inlet, sits just south of the Loyston Sea, one of the widest stretches of the reservoir.

Lake homes here can be reached by steep, winding drives, and some sit well below the road. Mention access when roofers call, along with how exposed the house is to wind off open water, since both affect fastening, material choice and labor.

sections.heading: Farms and valley communities
body: Away from the lake, State Routes 33, 61, 131 and 144 tie Maynardville to Luttrell, Plainview and Blaine. Luttrell sits in its own valley between Copper Ridge and Clinch Mountain. Electricity did not reach much of Union County until the mid-1950s, about two decades after Norris Dam was finished.

Roofing work here ranges from farmhouses and barns to manufactured homes and newer houses closer to the Knox County line, and one property may have several roofs worth quoting together. Ask for each structure as a separate line item so you can decide what to do now and what can wait.

sections.heading: Wind and falling trees
body: Recent National Weather Service storm reports from Union County describe trees and power lines coming down. On May 6, 2022, law enforcement reported trees and lines down in Luttrell, Sharps Chapel and Maynardville, and on January 12, 2023, trees fell widely across the county. In January 2024, a spot three miles south of Maynardville measured 8.3 inches of snow.
On wooded lots, a fallen limb can crack decking even when shingles look fine from the ground. After a storm, have a roofer look from the roof and from the attic for split boards or daylight.

roofing_notes: Norris Lake homes may need materials carried down steep drives; describe access up front.
Recent storms toppled trees around Luttrell, Sharps Chapel and Maynardville.
Barns and outbuildings can be quoted with the house as separate line items.
After a limb strike, have decking checked from the attic as well as the roof.

faqs.q: Will roofers come out to Sharps Chapel?
faqs.a: You can request quotes from anywhere in Union County, including the Sharps Chapel peninsula on Norris Lake, and matched roofers usually reach out within 24 to 48 hours. It helps to describe the drive and how far materials must be carried, because steep lake lots affect labor and the price.

faqs.q: What should I do if a tree limb hits my roof?
faqs.a: If water is getting in, cover the area or ask a roofer for an emergency tarp, then photograph the damage before anything is moved. Storms in recent years have brought down trees around Luttrell, Sharps Chapel and Maynardville, and limbs can crack decking even when shingles look intact, so ask for an attic check too.

faqs.q: Can I get one quote for my house and barn?
faqs.a: Ask for it. Mention every structure you want covered when roofers call, including barns, sheds and porches, and ask them to price each separately so you can compare. Some roofers focus on houses and others on metal farm buildings, so getting up to three quotes helps you find the right fit.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Grainger County, TN
hero_subtitle: From tomato farms below Clinch Mountain to lake homes on Cherokee Lake, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers serving Grainger County.
intro: Clinch Mountain splits Grainger County in two. South of it lie Rutledge, Bean Station, Blaine and Joppa, with Cherokee Lake along the southern edge; the northern section reaches the Clinch River arm of Norris Lake. Tomatoes have long been the leading crop, and the county counted more than 650 greenhouses in 2018. TVA's Cherokee Dam flooded the original Bean Station in 1942, and nearly half of the families relocated for that project came from Grainger County.

sections.heading: Big hail around Rutledge and Bean Station
body: Grainger County has taken some very large hail. On May 8, 2024, stones approaching 2.5 inches fell near Rutledge and 1.5-inch hail was reported in Bean Station, part of a storm the National Weather Service said produced hail in excess of baseball size across Grainger and Hamblen counties.

Hail that size can crack shingles, punch through skylights and dent metal roofs and greenhouse frames. After an event like that, get an inspection before the next heavy rain and document damage with dated photos. Tennessee law also lets you cancel a roofing contract within three business days of receiving your insurer's written notice that the claim is not covered.

sections.heading: Barns, greenhouses and farm roofs
body: With a farm economy, many properties have more than one roof. On February 6, 2025, a high-end EF-1 tornado with 110 mph winds tracked about four miles near Thorn Hill along Highway 131, damaging the roofs of several barns and outbuildings and destroying one large barn before ending on the side of Clinch Mountain near U.S. 25E.

If you want a farm building quoted with the house, say so up front and ask for separate line items. Metal panels on barns need different fasteners, trim and closures than a shingled house, so confirm the roofer does that kind of work.

sections.heading: Cherokee Lake and new building
body: Grainger County has no county-wide zoning, and new construction has been concentrated near the Cherokee Lake shoreline and around Bean Station and Blaine. That leaves a wide range of roofs, from new lake houses to older farmhouses and manufactured homes, so quotes can differ a lot in scope.

Lakeside property also catches wind: during the May 6, 2022 storms, a trained spotter documented wind damage at German Creek Marina near Bean Station. Ask about wind-rated materials and how edges and ridge vents will be secured.

roofing_notes: Hail near 2.5 inches fell around Rutledge in May 2024; check skylights and metal after storms.
Tennessee lets you cancel a roofing contract within 3 business days of an insurer's written denial.
Barns and outbuildings can be quoted alongside the house; ask for separate line items.
Cherokee Lake homes face open-water wind; ask how edges and ridges are fastened.

faqs.q: Can I back out of a roofing contract if insurance denies my hail claim?
faqs.a: Tennessee law gives you that right. If your insurer sends written notice that all or part of the claim is not covered, you can cancel the roofing contract by notifying the roofer before midnight on the third business day after receiving that notice. The cancellation should be signed and dated, and the roofer must return payments, with limited exceptions for emergency work.

faqs.q: How big was the May 2024 hail in Grainger County?
faqs.a: The National Weather Service received reports of hail up to 2.5 inches near Rutledge and 1.5 inches in Bean Station on May 8, 2024, and described stones larger than baseballs across Grainger and Hamblen counties. If your roof has not been inspected since, a roofer can check whether shingles were bruised or cracked.

faqs.q: Do roofers here work on barns and greenhouses?
faqs.a: Some do. When roofers contact you, list every structure you want quoted, along with its rough size and current material. Farm buildings with metal roofs need different fasteners and trim than a shingled house, so confirm the roofer handles that kind of work before you compare prices.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Campbell County, TN
hero_subtitle: From lake homes south of LaFollette to hillside houses in Jellico on the Kentucky line, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers in Campbell County.
intro: Campbell County sits where the Cumberland Mountains to the northwest meet the Ridge-and-Valley to the southeast. Elevations run from just under 1,000 feet near Norris Lake to 3,534 feet on Cross Mountain. Early in the 20th century, coal from the Jellico area made it Tennessee's largest coal-producing county. Today LaFollette sits in Powell Valley with Jacksboro and Caryville nearby along U.S. 25W, Norris Lake spreads to the south, and Jellico sits in the mountains on the Kentucky line.

sections.heading: Mountain towns and coal-era houses
body: Jellico grew quickly after rail service arrived in 1883 and mines spread through the Jellico Mountains. The town fills the Elk Creek valley across the bases and slopes of three steep hills, and Indian Mountain State Park was built on a reclaimed strip mine at its western edge. LaFollette was founded around 1890 by the LaFollette Coal, Iron, and Railway Company and incorporated in 1897.

Older houses in these towns may sit on hillsides with roofs layered over more than once. Expect a roofer to check the decking, and to plan around steep yards and narrow streets when placing ladders and a dumpster.

sections.heading: Wind on the ridges
body: During the March 30, 2022 high-wind event, the airport weather station near Jacksboro recorded a 62 mph gust, and in Jellico the wind blew part of a house's roof off. In December 2021, a fast-moving line of storms brought down trees in Jellico as well.

Exposed hillsides and ridge-top homes call for careful attention to starter courses, edge metal and ridge caps. If you are choosing between shingles and metal, ask each roofer for the product's wind rating and how it will be fastened.

sections.heading: Norris Lake and Cove Lake
body: Norris Lake, built by TVA in the 1930s, is the county's main body of water and dominates the area south of LaFollette. Cove Lake State Park near Caryville surrounds a smaller TVA-built recreational lake fed by Cove Creek. Homes and cabins along the coves deal with heavy tree cover, damp shade and steep access.

Hail reaches the county too: on May 6, 2022, a resident near Pioneer reported 1.25-inch hail along with trees and power lines down. After a storm like that, look for dented gutters and vents and get a roofer's opinion before calling your insurer.

roofing_notes: Hillside and ridge homes face strong gusts; ask about wind ratings and fastening.
Coal-era homes in Jellico and LaFollette may have several roof layers and older decking.
Cabins on Norris Lake coves can have steep, tight access for crews.
Hail of 1.25 inches was reported near Pioneer in May 2022.

faqs.q: How strong has the wind been in Campbell County?
faqs.a: Strong enough to strip roofing. On March 30, 2022, the airport weather station near Jacksboro measured a 62 mph gust, and in Jellico wind blew part of a house's roof off. Ask roofers how they fasten shingles or metal panels on exposed sites and what wind rating the product carries.

faqs.q: Do you serve Jellico and the rest of the county?
faqs.a: You can request free quotes from anywhere in Campbell County, including Jellico (37762), LaFollette (37766), Jacksboro (37757), Caryville (37714), Pioneer (37847) and the Campbell County side of Rocky Top. There is no obligation, and you can compare up to three roofers before choosing.

faqs.q: What should I know before reroofing an older house in LaFollette or Jellico?
faqs.a: Older homes in these coal-era towns may have more than one layer of shingles, board decking with gaps, or chimneys that are no longer used. Ask each roofer whether the quote includes a full tear-off, how they price replacing damaged decking, and what they will do with old chimneys and flashing.

h1: Free Roofing Quotes in Morgan County, TN
hero_subtitle: On the eastern edge of the Cumberland Plateau, from Wartburg and Coalfield to Deer Lodge and Rugby, compare up to 3 quotes from licensed, insured roofers.
intro: Morgan County lies on the eastern edge of the Cumberland Plateau, a place of rugged mountain terrain, cold streams and small towns. The Crab Orchard Mountains rise around Frozen Head State Park, the Obed Wild and Scenic River joins the Emory southwest of Wartburg, and U.S. 27 runs south to Harriman and I-40. Wartburg was founded in the mid-1840s by German and Swiss settlers, and Rugby, on the county's northwest side, was started in 1880 by English author Thomas Hughes.

sections.heading: Tornadoes on the plateau
body: Morgan County has been struck by two deadly tornadoes this century. On November 10, 2002, a tornado tore through Mossy Grove and Joyner, killing seven people and destroying dozens of homes. On February 6, 2025, an EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 135 mph tracked nearly 14 miles through the Deer Lodge area, destroying two mobile homes, damaging barns and outbuildings, and killing two people.

Manufactured homes and farm buildings fare worst in storms like these. If you own one, ask roofers about roof-over systems and fastening, and make sure the contractor has worked on manufactured homes before.

sections.heading: Snow and freeze-thaw
body: Winter storms can pile up snow here. In January 2024, a report a mile west-northwest of Wartburg measured 10 inches, with 6 inches at Petros and 8.5 inches west of Oliver Springs.

Heavy snow and repeated freezing and thawing find weak spots: ice backing up at the eaves, failed flashing around chimneys and soft decking. When comparing quotes, ask whether ice-and-water shield is included at the eaves and in valleys, and how many feet of it.

sections.heading: Historic Rugby and older communities
body: Rugby's historic district, listed on the National Register in 1972 as the Rugby Colony, is known for its Victorian architecture, and new homes in its Beacon Hill area must follow that style. Petros is home to the former Brushy Mountain State Penitentiary, which closed in 2009 and reopened in 2017 as a distillery and tour site.

Older houses in Wartburg, Sunbright, Oakdale and Coalfield, along with rural homes on large lots, often need a roofer willing to make the drive for a careful inspection. Ask each one how they handle multiple old layers and rotted decking, and whether those costs are in the price or billed as extras.

roofing_notes: Deer Lodge saw an EF-2 tornado in February 2025; have barns and outbuildings checked too.
Manufactured homes need a roofer experienced with roof-over systems.
Snow reached 10 inches near Wartburg in January 2024; ask about ice-and-water shield.
New homes in Rugby's Beacon Hill area must follow a Victorian style.

faqs.q: Has Morgan County had tornadoes recently?
faqs.a: Yes. On February 6, 2025, an EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 135 mph tracked nearly 14 miles through the Deer Lodge area, destroying two mobile homes and damaging barns and outbuildings. In November 2002, a tornado killed seven people around Mossy Grove and Joyner. After any severe storm, have roofs and outbuildings checked even if damage looks minor.

faqs.q: Can I get quotes for a manufactured home roof?
faqs.a: Yes. When roofers contact you, say the home is manufactured and describe the current roof, whether metal or shingles. Options and pricing differ from a site-built house, so ask whether the roofer regularly works on manufactured homes and which roof-over or replacement system they would use.

faqs.q: I own an older home near Rugby. Are there style rules?
faqs.a: Rugby Colony has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1972 and is known for Victorian buildings, and new homes in the Beacon Hill area must follow that Victorian style. If your house is in or near the historic area, ask Historic Rugby about any guidelines before choosing a roof color or material.
